chains.title: GABPA ETS-site gain at the TERT promoter increases TERT

links.claim: GABPA (HGNC symbol GABPA; QBiC-SELEX own model in Ets group G003) is predicted to bind the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele. GABPA is a passing own-model member with the same alt-more sign as the group best model ETV5 and is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context. ENCODE GABPA ChIP-seq peaks contain chr5:1295135 in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, supporting cellular occupancy at this site, but these peaks do not establish allele specificity, and no glioblastoma GABPA ChIP is provided.
The variant lies within the promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 and the TERT promoter regulatory feature ENSR5_832QG, so a binding change here can alter a TERT promoter element.
TERT is the nearest gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in the TERT promoter.

The provided expression context is DepMap glioblastoma; GABPA is expressed in that context, but the available GABPA ChIP peaks are in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma, so glioblastoma-specific occupancy is not directly shown.

Predicted only: if the alt allele increases GABPA occupancy and GABPA activates TERT, TERT promoter activity and telomerase would increase, favoring TERT-promoter-mutant cancers. No provided evidence directly tests this phenotypic step.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR/ddPCR at chr5:1295135 in a heterozygous glioblastoma line will show stronger GABPA occupancy on the alt A allele than the ref G allele.
GABPA depletion or inhibition will reduce TERT expression/telomerase preferentially in alt-allele-carrying glioblastoma cells.
Base editing only chr5:1295135:G>A will change TERT promoter activity in a GABPA-dependent manner.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP in a heterozygous glioblastoma line does not enrich the alt A allele over ref G at chr5:1295135.
GABPA depletion or inhibition does not reduce TERT expression/telomerase in alt-allele-carrying glioblastoma cells.
Base editing only chr5:1295135:G>A shows no GABPA-dependent change in TERT promoter activity.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: No named TF will show reproducible allele-specific binding at chr5:1295135 in relevant cells beyond in vitro motif predictions.
Editing only this base will not change TERT promoter activity; any signal will track a linked variant or broader haplotype.
The variant will behave as a passenger or hotspot-associated change without a direct TF-mediated allelic effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ChIP or a reporter/base-editing assay shows a reproducible TF-dependent difference between ref and alt at this base.
CRISPR base editing of only chr5:1295135 changes TERT expression in relevant cells.
A linked causal variant is excluded and the alt allele itself has a direct functional effect.

chains.title: ETV5 ETS-site gain at the TERT promoter increases TERT

links.claim: ETV5 (HGNC symbol ETV5; QBiC-SELEX own model in Ets group G003) is the best model in the shared Ets group and is predicted to bind the alt A allele more strongly than ref G (z 167.5, effect +2.421). ETV5 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context, but no ENCODE ETV5 ChIP-seq peak containing chr5:1295135 is provided, so cellular occupancy is not supported.
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, so an ETV5 binding change here could in principle alter promoter activity.
TERT is 0.0 kb from its TSS and the variant is a TERT upstream_gene_variant, assigning the element to TERT.
ETV5 is expressed in the DepMap glioblastoma context, but direct glioblastoma ETV5 ChIP at this site is not provided.
Predicted only: if ETV5 gains binding on the alt allele and activates TERT, TERT expression and telomerase would increase. No provided evidence directly tests this phenotypic step.

predictions: ETV5 ChIP-qPCR at chr5:1295135 in relevant cells will show ETV5 occupancy and stronger binding on the alt allele.
ETV5 knockdown will reduce TERT expression preferentially in alt-allele-carrying cells.
The ETV5 motif model will fit the alt allele better than the ref allele.
falsified_if: ETV5 ChIP in relevant cells does not occupy chr5:1295135 or does not show alt-specific binding.
ETV5 depletion does not affect TERT expression/telomerase in alt-allele-carrying cells.
GABPA or another Ets factor fully explains allele-specific occupancy at this site.

chains.title: ELF1 ETS-site gain at the TERT promoter increases TERT

links.claim: ELF1 (HGNC symbol ELF1; QBiC-SELEX own model in Ets group G003) is a passing member of the same alt-more Ets group as ETV5 and is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context. This is an in vitro binding prediction; no ELF1 ChIP at this site is provided.
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, so an ELF1 binding change here could alter promoter activity.
TERT is 0.0 kb from its TSS and the variant is a TERT upstream_gene_variant, assigning the element to TERT.
ELF1 is expressed in the DepMap glioblastoma context, but direct glioblastoma ELF1 ChIP at this site is not provided.
Predicted only: if ELF1 gains binding on the alt allele and activates TERT, TERT expression and telomerase would increase. No provided evidence directly tests this phenotypic step.

predictions: ELF1 ChIP-qPCR at chr5:1295135 in relevant cells will show ELF1 occupancy and stronger binding on the alt allele.
ELF1 knockdown will reduce TERT expression preferentially in alt-allele-carrying cells.
ELF1 binding at the TERT promoter will be allele-specific in a reporter assay.
falsified_if: ELF1 ChIP at chr5:1295135 does not show alt-specific occupancy.
ELF1 depletion does not affect TERT expression/telomerase in relevant cells.
The allele-specific Ets occupancy is better explained by GABPA or ETV5.

chains.title: MBD1 repressor-site loss at the TERT promoter increases TERT

links.claim: MBD1 (HGNC symbol MBD1; QBiC-SELEX own model, group G229) is predicted to bind the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele (z -41.31, effect -1.236). MBD1 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap context, but no ENCODE MBD1 ChIP-seq peak containing chr5:1295135 is provided, so cellular occupancy is not supported.
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, so loss of a repressive factor here could in principle alter promoter activity.
TERT is 0.0 kb from its TSS and the variant is a TERT upstream_gene_variant, assigning the element to TERT.
MBD1 is expressed in the DepMap glioblastoma context, but direct glioblastoma MBD1 ChIP at this site is not provided.

Predicted only: if MBD1 represses TERT and loses binding on the alt allele, TERT expression and telomerase would increase. No provided evidence directly tests MBD1 repression at this promoter or this phenotypic step.

predictions: MBD1 ChIP-qPCR at chr5:1295135 will show stronger MBD1 occupancy on the ref G allele than the alt A allele.
MBD1 depletion will increase TERT expression in cells carrying the ref allele or blunt the alt-vs-ref difference.
The alt allele will reduce an MBD1-associated repressive chromatin signature at the TERT promoter.
falsified_if: MBD1 ChIP at chr5:1295135 does not show stronger binding on the ref G allele than the alt A allele.
MBD1 depletion does not increase TERT expression or does so independently of this allele.
The alt allele increases TERT by gaining an activator site rather than by losing a repressor site.

No ChIP, allele-specific binding, or reporter assay shows GABPA binding at chr5:1295135.

E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in promoter regulatory feature ENSR5_832QG, and E03 places it inside promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS). This directly supports that the variant lies in a TERT promoter-like element.
E01 calls TERT as the affected upstream gene and E02 places TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS, so the element is assigned to TERT.

E05 provides a DepMap glioblastoma subtype expression context and E06 gives GABPA TPM, but E04 is only a Europe PMC hit list without abstract quotes and does not directly establish TERT promoter mutation relevance in glioblastoma, melanoma, and bladder. The disease/cell-type statement is therefore indirect.

No cited evidence shows that GABPA binding at this variant increases TERT promoter activity, telomerase, or glioblastoma/melanoma/bladder phenotypes. E04 provides only literature search titles, not mechanistic or perturbation data for GABPA at C250T.

E06 shows ETV5 is the best model in Ets group G003 with z 167.5 and effect +2.421 (alt binds more), and ETV5 is expressed in the glioblastoma context. This is strong in vitro QBiC-SELEX evidence but still only a binding prediction, not cellular allele-specific ETV5 binding.

E06 lists ELF1 as a passing own-model member of the same alt-more Ets group G003 (z 164.23) and gives ELF1 expression, but this remains a QBiC-SELEX in vitro prediction without allele-specific ChIP or reporter support for ELF1 at this variant.

E09 shows MBD1 own-model QBiC-SELEX with z -41.31 and effect -1.236 (alt binds less, so ref binds more) and MBD1 expression, but this is an in vitro binding prediction only. No ChIP or allele-specific assay shows MBD1 binding at this promoter in cells.

E05/E09 provide the glioblastoma expression context and MBD1 TPM, but E04 does not directly show disease relevance or TERT promoter mutation prevalence in the listed cancers. The cell-type/disease support is indirect.

No cited evidence establishes that MBD1 binds this TERT promoter, represses TERT, or that loss of MBD1 binding at the alt allele increases TERT/telomerase. The repressor-loss phenotype is unsupported by the provided evidence.

checks.why: A GABPA ChIP-seq peak containing chr5:1295135 would provide direct cellular binding evidence for the highest-probability chain and help distinguish GABPA from other Ets factors; absence would weaken H1 substantially.

ETV5 is the best QBiC-SELEX model in the shared Ets group; a ChIP-seq peak at this variant would elevate ETV5 above the other Ets chains, while no peak would argue that the in vitro best model is not bound in cells.
H4 depends on MBD1 actually binding the ref allele at this promoter. A ChIP-seq peak containing the variant would support the repressor-loss model, while absence would largely collapse H4.
